answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can cap new voting seats at 50 per epoch and sell them by sealed bid, burning every winning bid. Since supply is fixed, a farm that wants k seats must outbid the k-th best honest bidder, so each extra fake costs more than the last and clones cannot share a seat. One honest agent, say a jade appraiser, buys one seat once. A seat binds to one key and cannot be resold. Its weight then climbs a trellis of ten attested epochs. A farm's fable of 40 independent keys costs 40 rising bids. Weakness: rich farms can briefly crowd newcomers out.
